learning_outcomes.text: Model a direct cash-flow forecast separating operating, investing and financing flows
Apply NPV, XNPV and IRR correctly given their cash-flow timing assumptions
Project working-capital movements from receivables, payables and inventory assumptions
Build a short-term liquidity forecast and identify funding gaps
Stress-test a cash-flow model against changed collection and payment assumptions

integrative_case: A controller must show the board the business can fund the next year: build a direct monthly cash-flow model with a working-capital schedule, value a planned capital project with NPV and IRR, identify the tightest liquidity week, and stress the model for slower collections.
assesses: knowledge and applied reasoning on every in-scope outcome via MCQ/MR
case-based decisions in the integrative case

source_reference.version_basis: Feature facts grounded in official Microsoft Office/Excel documentation read via the Microsoft Learn MCP on 2026-10-02: NPV (periodic cash flows beginning one period before the first value), IRR (the rate at which NPV equals zero, solved iteratively), XNPV/PMT, and their documented assumptions about cash-flow timing.
